(353mm.) in leather fitted double violin case by W. E. Hill & Sons with outer canvas cover (3).  Sold with the Certificate of W. E. Hill & Sons, London, dated 30th November 1937 together with a letter dated 1st December 1937. Recorded in The Violin Makers of the Guarneri Family by Alfred, Arthur and W. Henry Hill. The history of this violin is related in the letter from Alfred Hill—“The instrument was originally purchased in Paris, about the year 1860, by a Mr Charles Finch, an excellent amateur, . . . Prior to the death of Mr Finch, about 1875, this violin passed to Mr John Adam an enthusiastic violin-lover who had the finest collection of Stradivari and Guarneri instruments in the country: owing, however, to the stress of financial difficulties he decided, in 1882, to dispose of his Collection which was then acquired by David Laurie of Glasgow, the principal international dealer of his day. The above violin was then sold to a Scottish amateur of the name of J. G. Orchar of Broughty Ferry who, prior to his death in 1897 bequeathed his small Collection comprising ‘Stradivaris’, and ‘Amati’ and this ‘Guarneri’ to the Museum at Broughty Ferry. The Authorities, however, deeming it unwise to preserve violins in glass cases had recourse to the Law and, in 1924, obtained permission to sell them, we being entrusted with their sale. Thus it happened that in 1926, this ‘Guarneri’ passed into the possession of Mr Rudolph Wurlitzer of Cincinnati who sold it to Mr John Taylor Roberts of Hartford, Connecticut. In 1929, however, it again passed into the possession of Mr Rudolph Wurlitzer by way of exchange . . .” [See COLOUR PLATE]
